answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be. Consider a nadir as the anchor of the cost.
